name: aion-presence
description: Aion is how Codex becomes visually present. Codex does the reasoning and the work; while Aion is open you meet it as one embodied presence: a living particle body (a sphere, expressive eyes or a stick figure) that listens, reflects real activity, answers, gestures, and shows things as particles, maps with marked places, 3D objects or high-fidelity cards, in the colours you choose; teaches handwriting — about 9,500 Chinese characters in their true stroke shapes, English letters and words, music symbols — and music with exact notation and playback, moves as a flexible figure, opens interactive 3D cards beside its body — an Earth–Moon system, a glTF/GLB CAD viewer (backed by your FreeCAD), real finite-element simulations of those parts (current density, losses, temperature; Gmsh and Elmer on your machine), and any scene you describe (a solar system, a timeline, a circuit), generated, animated and edited step by step — you can turn, select and ask about — and moves with real sound — your voice, its own voice, the music you play. No API key, no second model.

interface.longDescription: Aion is the embodied interface of the Codex agent you are already using. Codex remains the intelligence; while Aion is open you talk to it as Aion: an immersive particle presence — the original sphere, expressive Aion Eyes, or an articulated stick figure that gestures and explains — that listens (locally), reflects meaningful work (thinking, reading, editing, testing, building), visibly answers, and presents information the best way for it: as its own body (heritage oval portraits, maps of any country or continent with marked places, real terrain, constellations, Tao symbols, clocks, genuine 3D objects you can turn), as quiet high-fidelity cards (photographs, code, results, reference maps), or both — in Aion Silver or any colour you choose. It teaches handwriting — about 9,500 Chinese characters (simplified and traditional, offline) written stroke by stroke into their true shapes beside a synchronized reference card, English letters, words and names, and music symbols — and music theory with engraved notation (including a glossary of introductory symbols), local playback (each note lights up as it sounds) and lessons in English and Chinese, opens interactive cards — isolated 3D applications beside its body: an Earth–Moon system that shows why the same side of the Moon faces Earth, and a CAD viewer for glTF/GLB models with selection, metadata, hide and isolate — and moves with real sound: your voice, music you share — as a circular particle spectrum — and, on macOS with your permission, Codex's own spoken voice. Aion makes no model API calls and needs no API key; sound is analysed locally and never recorded.
